A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the active site of pyruvate-kinase is not rigid, but rather it has a conformational flexibility.

the active site is a very flexible site that is able to accommodate several different conformations of the substrate, and that the secondary site is a very rigid site that is able only to accommodate one conformation.
the ATP bound at the active site is not in the same conformation as the ATP bound at site II.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are multiple binding modes for Mg-ATP in the active site of the pyruvate kinases, and the active site of these enzymes is a dynamic structure that changes conformation depending on the binding mode of the ligands.
MgATP bound in the active site of pyruvate kinases is in a mixture of conformers that are similar to the conformers of free MgATP, and that these conformers do not change upon binding P-enolpyrvuate.
MgATP binds to the active and the secondary sites of pyruvate kinases with different conformations.
